newsitem.title: USA: NASD seen unlikely to waive muni rule for firm.
newsitem.headline: NASD seen unlikely to waive muni rule for firm.

text.p: The National Association of Securities Dealers will likely bar Morgan Stanley & Co. from doing negotiated bond business with Massachusetts after a bond executive improperly donated $1,000 to the state's governor, an NASD official said Tuesday.
A 1994 securities law bars municipal dealers that make contributions to issuer clients from doing business for two years with those governments.
The NASD has authority to grant exemptions from the rule, but will probably not do so, the NASD official said.
"I don't think there will be a waiver granted," said the NASD official, who asked not to be identified.
NASD only grants such waivers if "there is an extremely good reason for the violation," he said in a telephone interview.
The NASD official's comments came after Morgan Stanley announced that Peter Karches, head of its fixed-income department, contributed $1,000 to Massachusetts Gov. William Weld's U.S. Senate campaign.
Morgan Stanley, a unit of Morgan Stanely Group Inc., said Monday that Karches did not realise contributions to state or local officials running for federal office would be covered by the rule.
It added that the firm had withdrawn from any negotiated bond business with Massachusetts authorities while NASD reviewed its request for a waiver from the rule.
Reid Walker, associate director of media relations for NASD, had no comment on Morgan Stanley's request.
He noted, however, that NASD grants exemptions only under very limited circumstances. "All we can say is we haven't granted a waiver all year," Walker said.
